On Reading in the Margins

Readers have always written in the margins of books. Marginalia record a conversation between the reader and the text, and sometimes between readers across centuries.

The practice was common in medieval manuscripts, where scribes added glosses that explained difficult passages. Later readers responded to those glosses with their own notes, building layers of commentary.
